activities.title: Build the Agent Loop (Wednesday)
activities.description: Parts 1–4 of the notebook, on your own key:

steps.title: Define a tool
steps.description: A job description for Gemini (name, what it does, what inputs) plus the Python function that actually runs.

steps.title: Write the loop
steps.description: Send message + tools → model decides → your code runs the tool → result goes back → repeat until it answers.

steps.title: Watch it decide
steps.description: 7,394 × 8,261 reaches for the calculator. 'Capital of France' does not. Nobody wrote an if-statement.

steps.title: Chain three tools
steps.description: Calculator, stock lookup, company info: count the calls and watch results feed each other.

activities.title: Make It Enterprise-Grade (Wednesday, together)
activities.description: Part 5: the trust layer that separates a demo from a deployment:

steps.title: Retries and a circuit breaker
steps.description: Exponential backoff on 429s, a max-steps guard so it can never loop forever.

steps.title: Error propagation
steps.description: A failing tool returns its error to the model, which reports honestly instead of filling the gap.

steps.title: The approval gate
steps.description: The agent wants to send an email. HUMAN_IN_THE_LOOP decides. Flip it and approve one yourself.

steps.title: The audit log
steps.description: Every tool call, timestamped, as a table. What compliance asks for on day one.

activities.discussionNote: The loop is 40 lines. The trust layer around it is the product.

steps.description: Problem · user · 10× advantage · the one core flow. Feature lists are killed on sight.

steps.description: CRAFT the prompt in Lovable or Bolt, generate, test with real input, fix the #1 issue.

steps.title: Swap-test (5 min)
steps.description: Use a neighbor team's product. Write them one thing to fix.

steps.title: Publish
steps.description: Post your live link in the Canvas Session 4 discussion.

activities.title: Demo Day (Monday)
activities.description: Sixty seconds per team, live link, real input:

steps.title: Show, don't tell
steps.description: No slides, no 'imagine that'. Open the link and use it.

steps.title: Vote by hands
steps.description: Best problem–solution fit · Most delightful · Best UX.

steps.title: The only question
steps.description: Would a stranger use this tomorrow?

takeaways.text: A chatbot answers. An agent does. LLM + Tools + Loop + Memory — the model decides which tool, when, and whether it's done.
A tool is a Python function with a job description. Which tools to build is a business decision, not an engineering one.
The trust layer is the product. Retries, error propagation, a step limit, an approval gate, an audit log — day one, not after the incident.
Problem First, One Core Flow. A link a stranger can use beats any deck or spec.
Prototype before you buy. You can now build an MVP in an afternoon — cheaper than the meeting about it.
